hypothesis: For each of the eight canonical (failure_signature, minimal_lift) pairs from Extended-Program section 5.8 of The Structural Intelligence Conjecture, there is a finite hand-designed world on which the broken representation misses the target invariant, the lifted representation captures it, and the lift is minimal (Theorem RR-1); and two independent lifts on a product world compose to a joint lift that captures both invariants (Theorem RR-2).

controls.description: The check 'I factors through rep' iterates every pair of states and asserts rep(s)=rep(s') implies I(s)=I(s'); asserted in tests.
The minimality gate exhaustively drops every nonempty subset of added components; if any strict enlargement of R (below R') captures I, the gate fails; asserted in tests.

Theorem RR-2 is witnessed by composing the scalar->operator lift and the static->path-space lift on the product of the two toy worlds; the two lifts operate on disjoint slots and therefore commute by construction; asserted in tests.
There is no PRNG anywhere in the benchmark; every gate is a deterministic finite enumeration; asserted by the runtime signature (no seed field).

gates.criterion: For every one of the eight canonical pairs, the broken representation R misses the target invariant I on the pair's finite toy world (8/8).
For every one of the eight canonical pairs, the lifted representation R' captures the target invariant I on the pair's finite toy world (8/8).
For every one of the eight canonical pairs, no strictly smaller enlargement of R also captures I: for every nonempty subset D of the added components, R combined with (added minus D) misses I (8/8).

On the product of the scalar->operator world and the static->path-space world, the composed lift captures both sub-invariants and the composite invariant, is minimal (dropping any added feature breaks capture), and produces identical capture regardless of the ordering of the two lifts.
